item.title: Morning Brief: Friday, Nov 20
item.description:
Today at a glance: The UK and EU close a Brexit "reset" deal in Brussels, Russia hits three Kyiv bridges in one of the war's biggest strikes, the Senate passes permitting reform and again rejects an Iran war-powers resolution, and the White House fires its national cyber director after a week of outages.

Weather

  • Washington, DC: Sunny, high 69, low 42 tonight, nearly calm winds. No alerts. NWS
  • Boston, MA: Sunny, high 67 this morning, easing to about 61 this afternoon, low 45, west winds 6 to 12 mph. No alerts. NWS
  • Los Angeles, CA: Sunny, high 64, low 44, north-northwest winds 5 to 10 mph with gusts to 20 tonight. No alerts. NWS
  • Cape Canaveral, FL: Showers and thunderstorms (90% chance), high 77, low 68, northeast winds 15 to 20 mph gusting to 30. Another 2 to 3 inches of rain is possible, with storms tapering after 7 PM. A Flood Watch runs until 7 PM, a Flood Warning until 8:30 AM, and a High Surf Advisory through Saturday evening. Poor launch weather today. NWS
  • Boca Chica (Starbase), TX: Sunny, high 73, low 62, light north-northeast winds 5 to 10 mph. There's a Coastal Flood Advisory and rip current risk until 7 PM ET. Otherwise, benign conditions. NWS

Worth reading today

  1. The new Artemis plan shifts the burden onto Orion: Lockheed's Orion program manager explains to Ars what docking with Starship in high Earth orbit, and meeting Blue Moon in low lunar orbit, demands of the capsule. Ars Technica
  2. (poli sci) A wave, not a realignment: Using the SSRS 2026 Voter Poll, political scientists argue that independents, Gen Z and Latino voters powered the Democratic midterm sweep, but that both parties should read it as a warning rather than a lasting new coalition. The Conversation
  3. Congress and the coming crises: Foreign Affairs argues that the affordability agenda Democrats ran on is tied to wars in Europe and the Middle East, AI's power demands, and a national debt over $40 trillion. Foreign Affairs (paywall)
  4. Pentagon buys munitions without a plan: The public version of a classified GAO study finds DoD has no overarching plan linking munitions production to war-plan requirements. Defense News

US politics

  • Update, permitting reform passes the Senate: The bipartisan BAAJA permitting bill passed 62-33, with 14 Democrats and one independent voting yes, to speed approvals for power plants and data centers. It now goes to the House. Framing splits along familiar lines: Fox calls it Republicans "breaking through gridlock," the Post headline says it "weakens environmental laws," and the NYT says it's splitting the environmental movement. NPR · Axios
  • National cyber director fired after outages: Sean Cairncross is out, and Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies replaces him. CBS's sources say he was fired and that chief of staff Stephen Miller had long wanted him gone. This comes after a week of outages hitting Microsoft, air traffic control, banks and the NSA network. DHS Secretary Mullin says he's "98% confident" foreign actors weren't behind them. CBS News · Axios
  • Senate rejects Iran war-powers resolution, 48-51: This was the first vote since the midterms. Murkowski and Paul were the only Republicans voting yes, and Fetterman was the only Democrat voting no. Democrats are now looking at government funding as their next lever. ABC News · Fox News
  • Update, Alaska Senate: The Justice Department asked an appeals court to dismiss as moot its suit to block certification of Mary Peltola's win. She took 50.13%. Guardian · NYT (paywall)
  • CISA nominee won't call Jan. 6 an "attack": Michael LoSapio also wouldn't name the winner of the 2020 election at his confirmation hearing, which is part of the GOP rush to confirm nominees before January. AP via ABC News
  • Cornyn blocks a Trump judicial pick: The outgoing Texas senator won't back 37-year-old DOJ official T. Elliot Gaiser for a North Texas district seat, a day after a floor shouting match with Ted Cruz. Guardian
  • Oversight fight on both sides: Freshman Brandon Gill (backed by Whip Emmer) and Pat Fallon are vying to be the top Republican on House Oversight as Democrats prep investigations into Trump's family and advisers. Separately, incoming Judiciary Chair Jamie Raskin told the FBI, DOJ, DHS, ICE and BOP to preserve messages sent on apps like Signal. Axios · AP via WTOP
  • Trump pardons Pete Rose: The posthumous pardon covers Rose's 1990 tax conviction. It's largely symbolic and doesn't change his Hall of Fame status. BBC

Foreign affairs and defense

  • Russia hits three Kyiv bridges: Ballistic missiles struck the Podilsko-Voskresensky, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges, which are now closed, in what Zelensky called one of the war's most massive strikes. At least eight people were killed nationwide. It's retaliation for Ukraine's strikes on the Crimean Bridge. Poland is investigating a suspected airspace violation this morning. BBC · Politico Europe
  • Europe rehearses a postwar Ukraine force: Thousands of troops from 11 countries, led by France and the UK under the Coalition of the Willing, are drilling in southeastern Poland for a possible stabilization mission. AP via WTOP
  • Iran masses a tanker convoy at Kharg: Satellite and ship-tracking data show more than 14 tankers crewed and flagged to try to run the US blockade toward the Sea of Oman in the coming days. Washington has warned it will target vessels involved in such operations. Euronews
  • UK: Brexit reset deal is done: At the Brussels summit, No. 10 says the UK and EU agreed on food and drink (SPS) rules, emissions trading, and a youth mobility scheme, reportedly up to 100,000 a year each way. Tuition fees are still unresolved, and the EU is linking adoption to them. Farage says PM Andy Burnham has "no democratic mandate," and Badenoch accuses him of reopening Brexit divisions. Guardian · BBC
  • France's 2027 race takes shape: Former PM Dominique de Villepin declared his presidential run today. The Socialists ended talks with the Greens after Marine Tondelier said she was open to an alliance with Mélenchon. Le Monde (paywall)
  • Update, Spain debate: Sánchez and Feijóo clashed over corruption, housing, migration and this year's train disasters, with 55% of voters still unsure whether they'll vote on Nov. 29. A PP-Vox bloc is near half the vote. Politico Europe
  • Germany wants a European TikTok: Culture minister Wolfram Weimer says investors could put about €25B into buying 75 to 80% of TikTok's EU business. TikTok calls the idea "nonsense." Politico Europe
  • France and Sweden hold first joint nuclear-deterrence drill: Exercise Excalibur ran Nov. 16 to 18 under Macron's forward-deterrence initiative, with nuclear-capable Rafales and Gripens over northern Sweden. No weapons were involved. Defense News
  • Second source for Tomahawk motors: Raytheon picked Ursa Major and Avio USA to jointly produce Tomahawk solid rocket motors. No timeline or dollar value was disclosed. Breaking Defense

Space

  • SpaceX courts Democratic lobbyists: Public records show SpaceX retained five lobbyists from bipartisan firm Mehlman Consulting, several with deep Democratic ties, as the incoming majority eyes probes of Starlink in Ukraine, Pentagon dependence, and Musk conflicts. Fox News
  • BepiColombo nears Mercury orbit: After an eight-year, roughly 10 billion km trip, the ESA-JAXA mission is about to perform a 37-minute capture burn. Its two orbiters will separate a few weeks later. BBC
  • Update, Shenzhou-24: The Long March 2F carrying Tiangong's first foreign astronaut rolled out at Jiuquan. CMSA says launch is "in the coming days." Space.com
  • Google books New Glenn: Blue Origin will launch Project Suncatcher data-center satellites to Sun-synchronous orbit in 2029, as US heavy-lift capacity fills up through 2030. Ars Technica
  • CRS-35 Dragon heads home: Undocking from the ISS is set for about 12:05 PM ET today, with coverage from 11:45 AM. Splashdown off California is targeted for Saturday around 4:55 PM ET, depending on weather. Space.com
  • Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth: It got there at 5:16 AM ET on Nov. 18, after more than 49 years of travel, about 16.1 billion miles out. Humanity's farthest spacecraft is the first to do it. NASA
  • Poland expands military space: The MoD plans to buy radar-imaging and encrypted military-comms satellites, plus a passive radar for space surveillance. Breaking Defense
  • Starlink in Greenland: A Greenlandic lawmaker alleges Danish soldiers are bringing private Starlink terminals despite restrictions on locals using the service. European Spaceflight
  • Hayabusa2 drops its final landing: Ion-thruster trouble led JAXA to scrap the 2031 rendezvous with 1998 KY26 for a high-speed flyby of 2015 BM510. Space.com

Science and technology

  • Update, Anthropic's debut: Shares closed at $97.17 on the first day, about 17% above the $83 IPO price, valuing the company around $1.76T, while the Nasdaq fell nearly 2.3%. Bloomberg reports the stock slid about 5% after hours. BBC
  • California subpoenas Nvidia: AG Rob Bonta is probing whether Nvidia's or Huang's actions let China obtain advanced chips or confidential information, and whether investors were misled. BBC
  • Pancreatic cancer pill shows rare promise: In a 61-patient trial of daraxonrasib in advanced disease, tumours stopped growing in almost all patients, and cancer became undetectable in 1 in 12. Doctors stress it isn't a cure. Guardian
  • Toward a living CTE test: BU researchers report blood proteins in JAMA that could one day diagnose CTE in living patients. The study is small. WBUR
  • Liver kept alive seven weeks outside the body: A Sydney team's machine-perfusion "artificial body" set the record. Results are pending publication. MIT Technology Review
  • EU Commission hit by an AI-generated cyber campaign: It's the bloc's first reported AI-assisted attack, detected Oct. 22, with no evidence of a broad staff data breach. DW
  • Apple is building its own AI agent: A job listing describes an assistant that can browse, work across apps, write code and call services. The Verge

Entertainment

  • 3 Body Problem season 2 dated: Netflix's trailer sets the six-episode season for Jan. 14, 2027. Space.com
  • Steam Machine, no waitlist: Valve's 512GB model is now add-to-cart with 3 to 5 day delivery. The 2TB is out of stock, and Valve warns RAM shortages could squeeze future supply. The Verge
  • Update, GTA VI: Sensor Tower estimates 24.5M units and about $2.36B in preorders plus first-day sales, which the BBC says makes it likely the biggest entertainment launch ever. BBC
  • McDonagh on stage and screen: WBUR's critic makes the case for Martin McDonagh's Oscar-buzzed "Wild Horse Nine" (with John Malkovich) alongside a Boston revival of "The Beauty Queen of Leenane." WBUR

Sports

  • Patriots, on bye, take stock: The Globe tallies a season of injuries, now topped by Maye's lower-leg injury. Next up is at the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29 at 4:05 PM ET. Boston Globe (paywall)
  • Celtics (11-4) head west: They're at Sacramento Saturday at 10 PM ET and at Golden State Sunday at 8:30 PM ET. ESPN
  • Bruins (14-7-1) host the Capitals Saturday at 7 PM. ESPN
  • DC sports, Rock Creek Tennis Center gets a new landlord: Mark Ein's Rollingwood Sports signed a 60-year lease to run the aging DC Open venue and committed at least $25M to it. Washington Post (paywall)
  • Update, Pochettino's debut at Anfield: He wants "no fear" when 18th-place Manchester United visit fourth-place Liverpool Sunday, after only three days with the squad. Guardian
  • Saka may miss Christmas: Arteta says the thigh injury needs about four more weeks, with no surgery. Guardian
  • F1 Las Vegas GP: Russell topped a wet FP2 by 0.071s over Gasly, with Leclerc third, after rain wiped out FP1 times. Qualifying is tonight at 11 PM ET and the race is Saturday at 11 PM ET. Formula 1
  • F1 to hire full-time stewards: The FIA will start in 2027 and ramp up to 12 to 15 permanent stewards by 2028. Guardian

Local news

  • DC, Metro weighs cuts and fare hikes: WMATA is considering significant service cuts and higher fare increases to close a gap of more than $130M as it nears a "fiscal cliff." Washington Post (paywall)
  • DC, online casinos on the table: The Council takes up legalizing online poker, roulette and more next month, weighing about $50M in tax revenue against addiction risk. Washington Post (paywall)
  • Update, Trump's DC arch: Judge Chutkan extended her order blocking construction of the 250-foot arch for two more weeks. NPR
  • Boston, 100+ days of T shutdowns in 2027: The MBTA's proposed schedule is down from 274 days in 2024 and 132 so far this year. Boston Globe (paywall)
  • Update, Clancy case goes to the SJC: The full court will hear her double-jeopardy bid to dismiss, with arguments in January, ahead of the March retrial date. WBUR
  • Plymouth Thanksgiving fight in court: United American Indians of New England are seeking an order after the town dropped its customary stage for National Day of Mourning speakers. Boston Globe (paywall)
  • Northeast household spending jumps: It averaged $91,698 in 2025, about 10% more than in 2024 and nearly $10,000 above the national average (BLS). WBUR

item.title: Morning Brief: Thursday, Nov 19
item.description:
Today at a glance: Trump, Xi and Putin wrap a first-ever three-way summit with modest agreements, House Democrats back off a December shutdown fight over Iran, the world court finds Myanmar committed genocide, and ULA traces the Vulcan failure to fuel delivery, not the BE-4 engines.

Weather

  • Washington, DC: Sunny and mild, high 66, low 40 tonight, light winds. No alerts. NWS
  • Boston, MA: Sunny, high 67 early then easing to about 59 this afternoon, low 43. The Globe says a nice weekend ends with a storm late Sunday night. NWS · Boston Globe
  • Los Angeles, CA: Rain and a chance of thunderstorms until about 4 PM, high 65, low 46. Another 3/4 to 1 inch of rain is possible, and a Flood Watch runs until 6 PM PT. NWS
  • Cape Canaveral, FL: Showers and thunderstorms with heavy rain (3 to 4 inches possible today), high 77, low 70, east winds 20 mph gusting to 30. Flash Flood Warning this morning, Wind Advisory until 10 AM, Flood Watch through Friday evening, plus high surf. Poor launch weather through Friday. NWS
  • Boca Chica (Starbase), TX: Partly sunny with a 30% chance of showers before 4 PM, high 75, low 65, NNE winds 6 to 15 mph. High Surf Advisory until 6 PM CT and a Coastal Flood Advisory until Friday morning. NWS

Worth reading today

  1. Why the Vulcan failure matters beyond ULA: Eric Berger explains why clearing the BE-4 engine is a relief for Blue Origin's New Glenn and NASA, and why ULA still faces months on the ground. Ars Technica
  2. Xi's diplomatic moment and its risks: BBC analysis of what Beijing gains by hosting the US-China-Russia summit, and what could go wrong for it. BBC
  3. Inside the Nov. 13 FAA ground stop: A minute-by-minute reconstruction of "the hairiest 90 minutes" for air traffic controllers. WIRED (paywall)
  4. (poli sci) The Southern Democratic Party, transformed: Coastal Carolina political scientists Gibbs Knotts and Drew Kurlowski argue that Scott Colom's Mississippi win reflects a changed electorate, from Jim Crow disenfranchisement to Black voters at the party's core, more than a simple realignment. The Conversation

US politics

  • Democrats back off a shutdown over Iran: House Democrats signal they won't use the December funding deadline to force an end to the Iran war and would rather wait until they hold the majority in January. Even progressives like Jayapal are open to waiting. Semafor
  • "Reconciliation 3.0" fading: House Republicans say the Senate's $350B defense-heavy package is dead without spending cuts, and the HASC chair says it's "not going to happen." GOP leaders also had to pull a rule vote after 14 Republicans didn't show up, and the House leaves today for Thanksgiving. Axios · Breaking Defense
  • Musk regrets his midterm spending: The top individual donor of the cycle ($446M for Republicans) told DealBook the spending was "pretty foolish," said he's "not MAGA," and called Texas Gov.-elect Hinojosa likely "quite moderate." Democrats have floated probes of SpaceX's government contracts. BBC
  • 2028 is already starting: Buttigieg allies are launching an effort to back another presidential run. Politico
  • Update, Senate Democratic leader race: Senators are publicly picking sides between Schumer and Van Hollen, and Semafor reports tech antitrust would be high on Van Hollen's agenda. Semafor
  • FCC and Kalshi: Ted Cruz's committee approved Trump's FCC nominee 15-0 while Democrats boycotted the vote. Separately, the administration ordered Kalshi to stop taking bets on what words Trump will say. Ars Technica · Ars Technica

Foreign affairs and defense

  • Trump-Xi-Putin summit ends with modest deals: After more than an hour of three-way talks in Shenzhen, Russian officials and Chinese state media say the three agreed on UN reforms, boosting fuel supplies, and dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The declaration doesn't mention Ukraine or Iran. Arms-control experts call it, at best, the start of a process. AP via WTOP
  • Europe pushes back: UK Tory leader Badenoch called the summit "disturbing" and Poland's Tusk appeared to mock Trump's Putin remarks, as Ukraine's allies meet in Berlin. The UK is pledging 1,000 long-range strike drones (up to 1,000 km range) in a £260M winter package. Politico Europe · BBC · Guardian
  • Update, Kerch Bridge: A third Ukrainian strike in four days has halted rail traffic on Russia's bridge to Crimea. AP via WTOP
  • World court rules Myanmar committed genocide: For the first time, the ICJ has found a state responsible for genocide, ruling on the 2016-17 campaign against the Rohingya. It's seen as a precedent for South Africa's case against Israel, and there are fears the US could sanction ICJ judges. Guardian
  • Houthi missile debris hits Riyadh: A witness reported damage to the PIF Tower in the financial district. Saudi officials told allies the Houthi conflict could last six more months. Crude flows through Hormuz are about half of prewar levels this month (Kpler). AP via WTOP
  • Update, Gaza: Israel says it has completed its ground operation beyond the Yellow Line in central Gaza. BBC
  • Spain's race tightens: A new POLITICO/PF Global poll has the PP at 29.5%, the Socialists at 27.2%, and Vox at 19.6%, which makes a PP-Vox majority the likeliest outcome. Feijóo and Sánchez debate tonight, ahead of the Nov. 29 vote. Politico Europe
  • UK politics: James Cleverly will run as the Conservative candidate for London mayor, and the government plans to scrap the leasehold system in England and Wales. BBC · BBC
  • Hegseth signs Venezuela defense pact: In a surprise Caracas visit, Hegseth signed a deal with interim President Delcy Rodríguez covering intelligence sharing and joint training, calling Venezuela a "compliant security partner." He then went on to Colombia. DW · Euronews
  • Navy used expired munitions in the Iran war, says Navy Secretary nominee Hung Cao. Defense News

Space

Today at a glance: Trump, Xi and Putin wrap a first-ever three-way summit with modest agreements, House Democrats back off a December shutdown fight over Iran, the world court finds Myanmar committed genocide, and ULA traces the Vulcan failure to fuel delivery, not the BE-4 engines.

Weather

  • Washington, DC: Sunny and mild, high 66, low 40 tonight, light winds. No alerts. NWS
  • Boston, MA: Sunny, high 67 early then easing to about 59 this afternoon, low 43. The Globe says a nice weekend ends with a storm late Sunday night. NWS · Boston Globe
  • Los Angeles, CA: Rain and a chance of thunderstorms until about 4 PM, high 65, low 46. Another 3/4 to 1 inch of rain is possible, and a Flood Watch runs until 6 PM PT. NWS
  • Cape Canaveral, FL: Showers and thunderstorms with heavy rain (3 to 4 inches possible today), high 77, low 70, east winds 20 mph gusting to 30. Flash Flood Warning this morning, Wind Advisory until 10 AM, Flood Watch through Friday evening, plus high surf. Poor launch weather through Friday. NWS
  • Boca Chica (Starbase), TX: Partly sunny with a 30% chance of showers before 4 PM, high 75, low 65, NNE winds 6 to 15 mph. High Surf Advisory until 6 PM CT and a Coastal Flood Advisory until Friday morning. NWS

Worth reading today

  1. Why the Vulcan failure matters beyond ULA: Eric Berger explains why clearing the BE-4 engine is a relief for Blue Origin's New Glenn and NASA, and why ULA still faces months on the ground. Ars Technica
  2. Xi's diplomatic moment and its risks: BBC analysis of what Beijing gains by hosting the US-China-Russia summit, and what could go wrong for it. BBC
  3. Inside the Nov. 13 FAA ground stop: A minute-by-minute reconstruction of "the hairiest 90 minutes" for air traffic controllers. WIRED (paywall)
  4. (poli sci) The Southern Democratic Party, transformed: Coastal Carolina political scientists Gibbs Knotts and Drew Kurlowski argue that Scott Colom's Mississippi win reflects a changed electorate, from Jim Crow disenfranchisement to Black voters at the party's core, more than a simple realignment. The Conversation

US politics

  • Democrats back off a shutdown over Iran: House Democrats signal they won't use the December funding deadline to force an end to the Iran war and would rather wait until they hold the majority in January. Even progressives like Jayapal are open to waiting. Semafor
  • "Reconciliation 3.0" fading: House Republicans say the Senate's $350B defense-heavy package is dead without spending cuts, and the HASC chair says it's "not going to happen." GOP leaders also had to pull a rule vote after 14 Republicans didn't show up, and the House leaves today for Thanksgiving. Axios · Breaking Defense
  • Musk regrets his midterm spending: The top individual donor of the cycle ($446M for Republicans) told DealBook the spending was "pretty foolish," said he's "not MAGA," and called Texas Gov.-elect Hinojosa likely "quite moderate." Democrats have floated probes of SpaceX's government contracts. BBC
  • 2028 is already starting: Buttigieg allies are launching an effort to back another presidential run. Politico
  • Update, Senate Democratic leader race: Senators are publicly picking sides between Schumer and Van Hollen, and Semafor reports tech antitrust would be high on Van Hollen's agenda. Semafor
  • FCC and Kalshi: Ted Cruz's committee approved Trump's FCC nominee 15-0 while Democrats boycotted the vote. Separately, the administration ordered Kalshi to stop taking bets on what words Trump will say. Ars Technica · Ars Technica

Foreign affairs and defense

  • Trump-Xi-Putin summit ends with modest deals: After more than an hour of three-way talks in Shenzhen, Russian officials and Chinese state media say the three agreed on UN reforms, boosting fuel supplies, and dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The declaration doesn't mention Ukraine or Iran. Arms-control experts call it, at best, the start of a process. AP via WTOP
  • Europe pushes back: UK Tory leader Badenoch called the summit "disturbing" and Poland's Tusk appeared to mock Trump's Putin remarks, as Ukraine's allies meet in Berlin. The UK is pledging 1,000 long-range strike drones (up to 1,000 km range) in a £260M winter package. Politico Europe · BBC · Guardian
  • Update, Kerch Bridge: A third Ukrainian strike in four days has halted rail traffic on Russia's bridge to Crimea. AP via WTOP
  • World court rules Myanmar committed genocide: For the first time, the ICJ has found a state responsible for genocide, ruling on the 2016-17 campaign against the Rohingya. It's seen as a precedent for South Africa's case against Israel, and there are fears the US could sanction ICJ judges. Guardian
  • Houthi missile debris hits Riyadh: A witness reported damage to the PIF Tower in the financial district. Saudi officials told allies the Houthi conflict could last six more months. Crude flows through Hormuz are about half of prewar levels this month (Kpler). AP via WTOP
  • Update, Gaza: Israel says it has completed its ground operation beyond the Yellow Line in central Gaza. BBC
  • Spain's race tightens: A new POLITICO/PF Global poll has the PP at 29.5%, the Socialists at 27.2%, and Vox at 19.6%, which makes a PP-Vox majority the likeliest outcome. Feijóo and Sánchez debate tonight, ahead of the Nov. 29 vote. Politico Europe
  • UK politics: James Cleverly will run as the Conservative candidate for London mayor, and the government plans to scrap the leasehold system in England and Wales. BBC · BBC
  • Hegseth signs Venezuela defense pact: In a surprise Caracas visit, Hegseth signed a deal with interim President Delcy Rodríguez covering intelligence sharing and joint training, calling Venezuela a "compliant security partner." He then went on to Colombia. DW · Euronews
